 Social Security COLA 2027: How Much Will Your Monthly Check Increase and When Will Payments Start?
 By: Daniel Brooks 
 | 
 Editor: Matthew Reed 
 | 
 Contributor: Ethan Parker 
 November 12, 2026, 17:20 WITA · 5 min read 
 Close ad × 
 Advertisement 
 The Social Security Administration headquarters in Maryland. Millions of Americans will receive a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) in 2027, increasing monthly retirement and disability benefits. 
 BALTIMORE, Aktualita.co  - Millions of Americans receiving Social Security benefits will see larger monthly payments in 2027 after the federal government confirmed a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA), providing additional financial support as households continue to face rising everyday expenses. 
 The Social Security Administration (SSA) announced the increase on October 14, 2026, confirming that nearly 72 million Social Security beneficiaries will receive higher payments beginning in January 2027. 
 Advertisement 
 For the average retired worker, the adjustment translates into approximately $75 more per month, bringing the estimated monthly retirement benefit from $2,095 to $2,170. 
 Supplemental Security Income (SSI) recipients will see their adjusted payments earlier, beginning December 31, 2026. 
 The increase is designed to help beneficiaries maintain their purchasing power as inflation affects essential expenses, including groceries, housing, transportation, and healthcare. 
 How Much Will Social Security Benefits Increase in 2027? 
 The confirmed 3.6% COLA represents a larger adjustment than the 2.8% increase implemented for 2026. 
 However, the actual dollar increase will depend on each beneficiary's existing monthly payment. 
 According to the SSA's official 2027 COLA fact sheet, estimated average monthly benefits will change as follows: 
 Benefit category Before COLA January 2027 
 Average retired worker $2,095 $2,170 
 Retired couple, both receiving benefits $3,238 $3,355 
 Average disabled worker $1,642 $1,701 
 Aged widow or widower living alone $1,936 $2,005 
 For someone currently receiving $1,500 per month, a straightforward 3.6% calculation would produce approximately $54 in additional monthly benefits. 
 A beneficiary receiving $2,000 would see an estimated $72 increase, while a $2,500 monthly benefit would rise by approximately $90. 
 These calculations are illustrative. Individual payment amounts may differ because of benefit rounding, Medicare deductions, and other applicable adjustments. 
 Social Security Commissioner Frank J. Bisignano emphasized the significance of the annual increase in the agency's October announcement. 
 “Social Security will implement this cost-of-living adjustment for 76 million Americans, giving them greater financial stability,” said Commissioner Frank J. Bisignano. 
 When Will the 2027 COLA Payments Start? 
 The new COLA takes effect with Social Security benefits for December 2026, which are generally paid in January 2027. 
 For most retirement, survivor, and disability beneficiaries, the payment schedule depends on their date of birth. 
 Under the SSA's published 2027 payment calendar, the first regularly scheduled January payments will arrive on these dates: 
 January 13, 2027: Beneficiaries born between the 1st and 10th of any month. 
 January 20, 2027: Beneficiaries born between the 11th and 20th. 
 January 27, 2027: Beneficiaries born between the 21st and 31st. 
 An exception applies to people who began receiving Social Security benefits before May 1997 and certain individuals who receive both Social Security and SSI. 
 Their Social Security payments are generally scheduled for the third day of each month. Because January 3, 2027, falls on a Sunday and January 1 is a federal holiday, their January payments are scheduled to arrive early, on December 31, 2026. 
 Beneficiaries should review their individual payment schedule to determine exactly when their increased benefits will arrive. 
 SSI Recipients Will Receive Higher Payments in December 2026 
 Approximately 7.3 million Americans receiving Supplemental Security Income will also benefit from the 3.6% adjustment. 
 Unlike regular Social Security retirement benefits, SSI payments are typically issued on the first day of each month. 
 Because January 1, 2027, is a federal holiday, January's increased SSI payments will be distributed on December 31, 2026. 
 The maximum federal SSI payment for an eligible individual will increase from $994 in 2026 to $1,029 in 2027. 
 For an eligible couple, the maximum federal monthly payment will rise from $1,491 to $1,544. 
 Actual SSI benefits may be lower depending on income, living arrangements, and other eligibility factors. Some recipients may also qualify for state supplementary payments. 
 Will Medicare Premiums Reduce the COLA Increase? 
 Although the 3.6% COLA provides higher Social Security benefits, retirees should remember that Medicare premiums can affect how much money ultimately reaches their bank accounts. 
 Many beneficiaries have their Medicare Part B premiums automatically deducted from their monthly Social Security payments. 
 According to projections in the 2026 Medicare Trustees Report, the standard Part B premium could increase from $202.90 per month in 2026 to approximately $209.50 in 2027. 
 That projected increase of $6.60 per month would reduce the net amount beneficiaries receive from their COLA adjustment. 
 However, the $209.50 figure remains a projection rather than a confirmed premium for 2027 as of November 12, 2026. 
 The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services will determine the final amount, and individual deductions may vary. 
 How to Check Your New Social Security Benefit Amount 
 Beneficiaries do not need to submit a separate application to receive the 2027 COLA. The adjustment will be applied automatically to eligible payments. 
 The SSA will provide personalized COLA notices showing updated monthly benefits and applicable deductions. 
 Most beneficiaries with personal my Social Security accounts who have enrolled in paperless notices can view their updated information through the online Message Center beginning in late November 2026. 
 Individuals who want early online access must create their account and enroll in paperless notices by November 18, 2026. 
 Those who do not receive electronic notices will generally receive their updated benefit information by mail in December. 
 The personalized notice is particularly important for Medicare enrollees because it can show the difference between their increased gross benefit and the amount they will actually receive. 
 Why Social Security Payments Are Increasing 
 Social Security COLAs are determined using changes in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, commonly known as CPI-W. 
 The 2027 adjustment reflects inflation measured between the third quarters of 2025 and 2026. 
 Annual adjustments are intended to protect the purchasing power of retirement, disability, and survivor benefits rather than provide an increase unrelated to inflation. 
 Other Social Security thresholds will also change in 2027. 
 The maximum amount of annual earnings subject to Social Security payroll taxes will increase from $184,500 to $192,300. 
 Meanwhile, the annual earnings limit for beneficiaries who remain below full retirement age will rise to $25,560. 
 For retirees, however, the most immediate concern is the amount of money they will receive each month. 
 With the 3.6% COLA now officially confirmed, beneficiaries can begin planning their 2027 household budgets while awaiting their personalized notices. 
 The key dates are December 31, 2026, for increased SSI payments and certain early Social Security payments, followed by the regular January 2027 Social Security payment schedule.
